reading.body:
CyrusOne's Durham campus publishes 40 MW of IT capacity across 420,000 square feet in two buildings, accounting for 80 percent of North Carolina's disclosed data center power capacity.

The facility consists of DUR1, an operational building with 92,320 square feet of raised floor across eleven data halls, and DUR2, a shell building delivered in 2025 with no capacity yet specified. At standard colocation density of 95 watts per square foot, this footprint could hold roughly 400 racks, though AI training workloads typically require substantially higher power density and would reduce that count significantly. The operator publishes no information about electrical infrastructure, cooling capability, or accelerator support for either building.

Durham sits within Research Triangle Park, a region with established technology infrastructure and university proximity. The presence of a recently completed shell building suggests potential for expansion, but whether DUR2 will be equipped for modern accelerator workloads or remains speculatively leased is not disclosed. The campus's relevance to AI compute scaling depends entirely on power supply capability and cooling design, neither of which the operator has published.

North Carolina has nineteen mapped data centers, but only five disclose power figures totaling 50 MW. This Durham cluster's dominance of published state capacity reflects operator transparency rather than actual footprint, leaving the true power base in the state unknown.
